title: Chapter 81
content:
His stomach was churning in violent knots, and his head felt as though someone had driven a railroad spike straight through his temples.

Forcing his heavy lids open, the mere thought of twitching a muscle felt utterly exhausting. Judging by the tangled bird's nest of bedsheets, he had spent the night thrashing in an absolute frenzy, ultimately waking up sprawled upside down across the mattress.

Groaning, Jakyeong pushed himself upright—only for his eyes to bulge in sheer disbelief.

Stacked squarely against the bedroom door was the heavy living room sofa.

"What the...?"

He rubbed his eyes, convinced he was hallucinating. He remembered knocking back drinks in the second-floor lounge with Wang Han and Wang Ryun until late, but beyond that, the night was a total, impenetrable blackout.

Sliding off the mattress, he cautiously scanned the suite. Nothing else appeared visibly out of place.

How in the world did that heavy sectional get in here?

Needing to shock his senses awake, he stumbled into the bathroom. Leaning over the marble vanity, he swept back his dark bangs.

Right in the dead center of his forehead sat a distinct, dark purple knot.

What the hell is this? Did I take a drunken header into a wall?

Looking down, fresh scrapes and mottled bruises colored his knees and forearms as well.

Just what kind of catastrophic disaster did I unleash last night?

He scrubbed down thoroughly under a steaming shower, plastered fresh pain-relief patches over the vivid constellation of hickeys Kang Il-hyun had left across his collarbones, and pulled on clean clothes. After wrestling the heavy sofa back into its rightful place in the lounge, he eased the bedroom door open with quiet apprehension.

Contrary to his worst fears, the second-floor corridor was pristine and serene. The cocktail glasses and stray liquor bottles from the night before had already been swept clean.

Letting out a quiet breath of relief, he descended the grand staircase. Rounding the corner, hushed murmurs drifted from the kitchen.

Before he could step inside, the senior housekeeper appeared, greeting him with a warm, maternal smile. "Is your stomach holding up, Master Ja-kyeong?"

Jakyeong gave a stiff, sheepish nod. "Yes, ma'am."

"Shall I brew you some spicy hangover soup?"

"No, that's alright. Whatever's ready is fine."

Stepping into the dining room, he found Wang Han and Wang Ryun seated at the table, quietly working their way through breakfast. The atmosphere around them was strangely tense. Jakyeong silently mouthed, What's going on? but the brothers merely averted their eyes, shaking their heads in synchronized evasion.

The housekeeper returned, setting down a steaming porcelain mug of warm honey water instead of juice. "Drink this to soothe your stomach before eating. Your breakfast will be out shortly."

Jakyeong settled into his seat, clutching the warm ceramic. Beside him, Ryun was dipping a roll into his soup, his cheeks violently twitching as he bit his lower lip to suppress a tidal wave of hysterical laughter.

An ominous dread began crawling up Jakyeong's spine.

Before he could corner his brother for an explanation, heavy, measured footsteps echoed from the foyer.

It was well past standard corporate commute hours, yet Kang Il-hyun strode casually into the dining room.

Jakyeong turned to offer a polite nod, only for his jaw to slacken.

Plastered squarely across the bridge of Il-hyun's nose was a pristine white medical bandage.

As Jakyeong stared in stunned silence, Il-hyun met his gaze, flashing a radiant, effortless smile.

"Good morning, gentlemen."

Il-hyun pulled out the chair directly adjacent to Jakyeong, settling down with relaxed poise.

As if on cue, Han and Ryun bolted upright from their seats, snatching their remaining rolls in one swift motion.

"Thank you for the wonderful meal, ma'am!"

Il-hyun casually extended an open hand, gesturing toward their empty chairs. "Now, now. The primary material witnesses shouldn't run off before court is in session."

Witnesses?

Il-hyun shifted his posture, squaring his broad shoulders to face Jakyeong's profile, casually resting a tailored forearm along the back of Jakyeong’s chair.

As the man leaned uncomfortably close, Jakyeong subtly inched his upper body backward against the wood.

"W-What is it?"

"Nothing to say to me this morning?"

Say to you? About what?

"What... happened to your nose?" Jakyeong asked cautiously.

Il-hyun wrinkled his brow with a pained, dramatic wince. "I suffered a vicious, unprovoked ambush by a feral cat last night."

Jakyeong’s brow knit in total confusion. A feral cat?

His eyes darted across the table. Han and Ryun were squirming in their seats, looking everywhere except at him. Reading the room, an icy chill washed over him. Did I really do that? Did I get blackout drunk and pick a fistfight?

No matter how hard he scraped the bottom of his memory, the canvas remained completely blank.

Testing the waters, he whispered timidly, "Did... did I do that?"

Il-hyun offered no verbal reply.

Instead, he reached up, loosening the knot of his silk necktie and undoing the top three buttons of his crisp dress shirt. Around his throat and collarbones lay an angry patchwork of mottled, dark crimson bruises.

"Don't tell me you've wiped this from your memory as well?"

Jakyeong’s jaw dropped. "Wait... me...?"

The moment the words cleared his lips, Il-hyun gave a sharp flick of his fingers.

Standing quietly near the credenza, Park Tae-soo stepped forward, presenting a sleek digital tablet. Tae-soo woke the screen and tapped play.

High-definition, full-color security footage filled the display.

The timestamp burned in the corner read 01:15 AM from the second-floor lounge.

On screen, the two men were violently shoving and grappling in the center of the room. Jakyeong threw a lightning-fast right cross, which Il-hyun ducked with practiced ease—but what followed was pure carnage.

The two went crashing onto the Persian rug in a tangled heap, where Jakyeong hooked his long legs over Il-hyun's shoulders, locking his ankles into a textbook, lethal figure-four leg scissors choke around the CEO's throat.

Faced with a full-body lower-limb chokehold rather than a standard arm triangle, even a combatant of Il-hyun's caliber had been entirely neutralized, violently thrashing across the floor in a desperate bid to break the hold.

The second the choke finally slipped, the video showed Jakyeong scrambling to his feet and sprinting into his suite like a startled rabbit.

Standing on screen with his hair wildly disheveled, Il-hyun had planted a hand on his hip, brushing the dark strands from his forehead with an expression of pure, murderous incredulity.

Even through a glass screen, the seething fury radiating from the man was palpable.

Jakyeong sat frozen with a piece of toast hanging from his lips, staring at the playback in horrified fascination.

Beside him, Il-hyun’s voice purred with silky amusement. "Care to hear the audio recording? It's significantly more passionate."

He swiped to the next file, and their voices echoed through the tablet's speakers in crystal-clear fidelity:

[Stop playing childish games and tell me exactly why you're pissed off!]
The deep, authoritative baritone belonged unmistakably to Kang Il-hyun.

[Fuck off, you bastard! Take one more step toward me and I'll kill you!]
Jakyeong’s recorded voice was practically spitting venom.

[I spoil you rotten, and you think that gives you license to crawl all over my head?]

[When did I ever ask you to spoil me, you lunatic?!]

[Come over here while I'm still asking nicely.]

[No! You ancient, perverted fossil!]

Cough.

Jakyeong’s eyes widened so fast they nearly popped from his skull.

In the audio playback, a suffocating, dead silence had descended over the room.

A moment later, Il-hyun's voice had returned—thick with stunned, wounded disbelief:

[Ancient... what did you call me?]

[An old, decrepit fossil!]

Sitting beside him in the flesh, Kang Il-hyun ground his molars together with an audible crunch.

Jakyeong carefully removed the toast from his mouth, placed it daintily onto his porcelain plate, and folded his hands neatly over his knees in a posture of pure, unadulterated penitence.

Holy shit. I've committed a capital offense.

Il-hyun turned his head, calling out to his security chief. "Tae-soo. Do I strike you as an ancient fossil?"

"Not in the slightest, President Kang," Tae-soo answered instantly, without a flicker of hesitation.

Jakyeong sneered internally. Loyal, but a shameless liar. Il-hyun had undoubtedly interrogated the housekeeper and the Wang brothers earlier, and all three had predictably offered identical, cowardly denials. When they first met, the man had claimed to be twenty-nine—a figure Jakyeong had found biologically impossible to believe. Now that the man had turned thirty, he looked marginally closer to a human being, though he'd likely only pass for his true age once he hit thirty-five.

Still, corporate age semantics were the least of his concerns.

Just as Jakyeong opened his mouth to offer a groveling apology, Il-hyun tapped the screen again.

Horrific, wet choking sounds erupted from the speakers as Il-hyun gasped for air under the leg lock. Cold sweat broke out across the back of Jakyeong's neck.

Finally slipping the hold, Il-hyun’s raspy, lethal growl bled through the speakers:

[Darling... are you genuinely trying to commit murder right now?]

Jakyeong’s recorded voice shrieked back with unhinged, hysterical fury:

[How do you like it, huh?! Sucks getting choked half to death, doesn't it?! Lay another finger on my throat and I'll pin you down, shove my foot up your ass, and stomp your windpipe flat!]

Click.

Unable to stomach another second, Jakyeong squeezed his eyes shut.

Il-hyun paused the file and set the tablet flat on the mahogany table. Propping his chin on his knuckles, he beamed at Jakyeong with terrifying, grandfatherly warmth.

"Does your memory serve you now?"

"I... I am deeply sorry, President Kang..."

"I was on the verge of meeting my maker last night, darling."

"I am truly, sincerely sorry..."

"No need for apologies," Il-hyun said, his voice dripping with tragic melancholy. "Thanks to you, I had the privilege of reuniting briefly with my late mother on the other side."

"..."

"Her complexion was remarkably vibrant. Quite a relief, really."

Il-hyun offered a faint, sorrowful smile, leaving Jakyeong entirely speechless. Given the man's notoriously explosive temper, waking up with all four limbs still attached was a statistical miracle. Jakyeong kept his chin tucked against his sternum like a condemned felon awaiting the executioner's blade.

The dining room had fallen into a tomb-like silence; across the table, not even the sound of his brothers breathing could be heard.

Il-hyun’s long fingers tapped rhythmically against the edge of the table: Tap, tap, tap.

He reached out, gently tucking a stray lock of dark hair behind Jakyeong’s ear. The touch was disarmingly tender.

"Let us dispense with the empty apologies. Why don't you tell me, in your own words, why you threw such a magnificent tantrum?"

Jakyeong kept his lips pressed into a thin line.

"Confess honestly, and I might consider full absolution."

"...I apologize. I genuinely have zero recollection of the event..."

"Think back carefully. There is always a catalyst."

"..."

"After all, I hardly take you for the sort of unhinged delinquent who gets blackout drunk and brawls with random strangers."

It was bizarre. The man was methodically laying out every offense, yet he looked entirely pleased with himself. That easy, smug grin was infinitely more terrifying than an outright beating. Jakyeong discreetly slid his steak knife and fork a few inches further away across the tablecloth.

"I... truly don't remember..."

A spark of playful mischief danced behind Il-hyun's dark irises.

Jakyeong scrambled for an out. "I... I get aggressive when I drink. My brothers can attest to it."

He spun a desperate, blatant lie. In truth, Jakyeong had only ever blacked out from alcohol once in his entire life—back when he was eighteen years old. Feeling the dry bread sticking heavily to his throat, he snatched his glass of ice water for relief.

He took a large, desperate gulp—

"Did it really break your heart that much to see me at a hotel with another woman?"

PFFT—!

The mouthful of ice water sprayed in a violent, aerosolized mist directly across Kang Il-hyun’s face.

Park Tae-soo stepped forward in an instant, offering a clean linen handkerchief.

Dabbing the moisture from his eyelids, Il-hyun broke into a deep, unrestrained chuckle, looking thoroughly, ecstatically delighted.

Jakyeong sat paralyzed with his mouth hanging open, his head whipping toward his brothers.

Han and Ryun executed a synchronized, guilty pivot, intensely studying the floral molding on the far wall. Those treacherous bastards snitched.

Wiping his chin dry, Il-hyun leaned his upper body across the table, closing the distance until their noses nearly brushed.

"Tell me, darling. Was the sight truly offensive enough to warrant strangling the life out of me?"

The triumphant grin stretched wider by the second.

Jakyeong’s upper lip quivered in frantic, cornered panic. Had he been furious yesterday? Undeniably. But he hadn't been enraged at the sight of Kang Il-hyun escorting some glamorous woman—he had been furious at himself for feeling an inexplicable, sour knot twist in his chest at the visual.

It wasn't jealousy. It couldn't possibly be jealousy.

"I completely understand," Il-hyun purred, a brief, lethal shadow flickering across his gaze before vanishing. "Had our roles been reversed, I would have butchered you and your companion on the spot."

"I have no idea what you're talking about..." Jakyeong stammered weakly.

Il-hyun picked up the tablet once more. "This won't do. Since you insist on denying it, I suppose I must provide the conclusive audio evidence."

Jakyeong went stark white. There is no earthly way I confessed to being jealous out loud.

"You're lying..."

"Let us listen and find out."

The instant Il-hyun’s thumb hovered over the screen, Jakyeong surged out of his chair. He snatched the tablet right out of Il-hyun's hands, wheeled around, and sprinted up the grand staircase like a track star.

He slammed his bedroom door shut, threw the deadbolts, and collapsed against the hardwood, gasping for air.

Unlocking the display, he frantically tore through the media storage. Aside from the CCTV footage and the single audio clip played downstairs, the directory was completely empty.

He scrubbed through the entire audio recording once more—not a single syllable about jealousy had escaped his lips.

Jakyeong sat on the floor clutching the tablet, his entire frame trembling with righteous, mortified fury. I got played. Completely and utterly conned.

Bzzzt.

The phone in his pocket chimed with an incoming text from My Darling ♥.

[Since you seem too shy to show your face downstairs, I'll have the staff send your breakfast up.]

He could practically see the bastard’s smug, triumphant grin through the glass. Grinding his teeth, a second chime followed immediately:

[Make sure you tell me in bed tonight just how jealous you were. ♥]
